description: One piece of work somebody has to go and do, carrying the evidence its completion has to produce. Compliance-native from the first field: a task cannot be created without stating what evidence closing it requires, and completing it writes the compliance record that dismisses the alert it came from.

fields.description: What a foreman calls it out loud: 'Habitability walk — MC-Cabin-01'. The docname is a sequence, because the same walk happens again next year and a name-as-key would collide with its own history.
fields.label: Task

fields.description:
The kind of work, which is what a skill filter and a dispatch board group on. Chosen so a whole type can be worked in one trip round the operation.

SCOUTING ARRIVED IN v0.115.0 and is deliberately its own type rather than an Inspection. An Inspection produces a pass/fail against a written standard; a scouting round produces a MEASUREMENT — a count, a growth stage, a Brix — that is compared to a threshold somewhere else. Folding it into Inspection would put every maturity walk on the compliance board and make the two impossible to filter apart on the handset, which is the one thing the type is for.
fields.label: Task Type
fields.options:
Inspection
Test
Spray
Repair
Harvest
Scouting
Training
Compliance-Audit
Hiring
Housing-Cleanup
Water-Sampling
Other

fields.description: How this task came into being. compliance_rule: generated from a compliance alert. foreman_dispatch: raised by a foreman from the Desk or MCP. field_reported: a worker in the field flagged a problem on the spot. worker_self_pick_from_pool: a worker picked it from the pool. Existing tasks default to compliance_rule.
fields.label: Origin

fields.description: Where the work has got to. Draft is not yet dispatchable; Available is in the pool; Claimed has somebody's name on it; In-Progress means they are stood in front of it; PAUSED means they were interrupted and are coming back — the task is still theirs and its clock is stopped; Awaiting-Review means it was done AND the record it produced needs somebody to look at it; Completed, Rejected, Cancelled and MERGED are terminal. Merged is the one that names another record: a duplicate folded into a primary task keeps its history and points at where the work actually went. This is the field the Kanban board columns are built from.
fields.label: State
fields.options:
Draft
Available
Claimed
In-Progress
Paused
Awaiting-Review
Completed
Rejected
Cancelled
Merged

fields.description: How soon. Critical is reserved for work whose absence is already unlawful — an expired licence, a failed CO detector in an occupied cabin. A board where everything is Critical is a board nobody reads.
fields.label: Urgency

fields.description: Whose operation the work belongs to. Filled in from the location where the location knows, because a dispatch board is read one company at a time.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: Which register the place is in: Parcel, Field, Irrigation Zone or Housing Unit. A Link to DocType rather than free text, so the Dynamic Link below resolves and the Desk can click through to the ground the work happens on.
fields.label: Location DocType

fields.description: The cabin, block, zone or parcel. A task with no location is legitimate — a certificate renewal happens at a desk — but a task about a place that does not name it cannot be routed to whoever is already stood there.
fields.label: Location

fields.description: What somebody has to be able to do: 'camp_maintenance', 'applicator_license', 'water_sampling', 'electrical_licensed'. Free text, because the skills an operation recognises are its own — the pool query matches on it, it is not validated against a list this app invented.
fields.label: Skill Required

fields.description: Dispatched means a foreman picks the person — specialised, licensed or safety-critical work where the named holder matters. Self-pick means workers take it from the pool. Either means both doors are open, which is right for most general labour.
fields.label: Dispatch Mode

fields.description: The Employee id currently holding this task, blank while it sits in the pool. DATA AND NOT A LINK, for the same reason Housing Assignment.employee is: Frappe HR is not a dependency of this app, and a Link would make the whole doctype fail to migrate on a site without it. It is validated against the Employee register wherever there is one.
fields.label: Assigned To
Farm Shift
fields.description: The shift this work belongs to. NOT a duplicate of the assignment's own shift link: this one says which shift the job was RAISED FOR, and the assignment's says which shift it was actually DONE ON. A spray task dispatched for the morning shift and finished on the afternoon's is two different facts, and a re-entry-interval question needs both.
How long it should take, in minutes. Used to plan a day, and compared against the actual on the assignment afterwards — which is how an estimate stops being a guess somebody made once.
fields.label: Estimated Duration (Minutes)

fields.description: The Compliance Alert that produced this task, blank when a foreman raised it out of the operation's own needs. THIS FIELD IS WHAT CLOSES THE LOOP: it is what generate_tasks_from_compliance_alerts checks to stay idempotent, and it is what lets an operation report what fraction of its alerts ever became work somebody was actually sent to do.
fields.label: Source Alert

fields.description: A work order in some other system this task answers. Data rather than a Link because the doctype it would point at does not exist yet on any site; when it does, this becomes the migration's join column.
fields.label: Source Work Order

fields.description: The Inspection Session this task is, where it is one. v0.21.0. A task carrying it is a MULTI-SECTION VISIT — one card on the board, one claim, one trip, and a sectioned form behind it that produces several compliance records. Blank is the ordinary case and means exactly what it always meant: one task, one piece of work, one record. THE TASK IS STILL THE DISPATCH ATOM either way — it is what a worker claims, what the concurrent-claim limit counts, and what the Kanban board shows. The session is the form behind the card, never a second kind of card beside it.
fields.label: Inspection Session

fields.description: The Farm Task Template this task was raised from, blank for one somebody raised by hand. v0.41.0. PROVENANCE AND NOT A LOOKUP: everything the task needs was COPIED off the template at creation — the type, the skill, the duration, the dispatch mode, the evidence contract, the record it produces, the instructions and the checklist — so this link is read to answer 'where did this shape come from', never to work out what the task requires. That is what makes editing a template safe: it changes what future tasks look like and touches nothing already raised.
fields.label: Template

fields.description: The record this task is ABOUT, where it is about one — the I-9 Form whose Section 2 needs signing, the W-4 waiting on a signature. v0.55.0. NOT `location`: a location is somewhere a worker can be SENT and is what the pool listing filters on, and an I-9 is not a place. This is the document whoever completes the task has to open, and it is what collect_form_signature reads to find the task a signature answers.
fields.label: About DocType

fields.description: The docname of the record above. A Dynamic Link, so the Desk clicks straight through to the form that needs the signature and a phone can open it without a second lookup.
fields.label: About Record

fields.description: The Asset Register record this task is about, where it is about one. A broken valve, a cabin window, a sprayer hose — any tagged asset a worker can scan. When present, the task appears in the asset's history timeline and the skill_required can be auto-filled from the asset type.
fields.label: Asset

fields.description: The Employee who flagged this problem in the field, distinct from whoever is assigned to fix it. Blank for tasks that did not originate from a field report. DATA AND NOT A LINK, for the same reason assigned_to is: Frappe HR is not a dependency.
fields.label: Reported By

fields.description: When the field report was raised — the moment the worker tapped 'Report a problem'. Distinct from creation, which is when the server processed it.
fields.label: Reported At

fields.description: When the thing being reported was actually SEEN, where that is not when it was filed. A picker who notices a broken line at first light and reports it at the tailgate two hours later has one fact and two times, and until this column existed the earlier one was prose inside the description. DELIBERATELY NOT reported_at: that stamp is the moment the report reached the server, it is the column report_field_task's five-per-hour rate limit counts on, and a caller who could set it could file a hundred reports dated an hour ago. So this one is caller-settable and that one never is.
fields.label: Observed At

fields.description: The 'before' photo the worker took at flag time: what the problem looked like before anybody was sent to fix it. Separate from completion evidence, which is the 'after'.
fields.label: Report Photo

fields.description: JSON: which of photos, signature, findings_text and witness a completion has to carry. REQUIRED AT CREATION AND THE WHOLE POINT OF THE DOCTYPE. A task that does not say what closing it requires is a task that gets closed with a tick in a box, and a tick in a box is what an auditor is trained to disbelieve. complete_farm_task refuses a submission that does not meet it.
fields.label: Evidence Required

fields.description: JSON: the checklist SNAPSHOTTED off the template at creation, with each item's done state beside it — {"items": [{"item_name": "…", "required": true, "evidence_type": "Photo", "sort_order": 1, "done": false, "note": ""}]}. v0.41.0. THE SNAPSHOT AND THE STATUS ARE ONE FIELD ON PURPOSE, and that is a database decision worth defending: two fields would let a task's list of items and its list of ticks drift apart, and a third table would be table sprawl in exchange for a list that is never queried across tasks. THE SNAPSHOT IS WHY EDITING A TEMPLATE IS SAFE — a worker halfway through a five-item walk whose template lost an item does not find their evidence attached to a list that no longer contains it. `{"items": []}` is the ordinary case: most tasks have no checklist. complete_farm_task refuses a completion with a required item unticked.
fields.label: Checklist Status

fields.description: The DocType this task's completion creates: 'Housing Inspection', 'Detector Test', 'Water Test'. Refused at creation if the site does not have it, because a task promising a record nobody can write is a promise that fails in front of a worker stood in a cabin.
fields.label: Creates Record

fields.description: The record the completion actually produced, once it has. Read with `creates_record` as its doctype.
fields.label: Produced Record

fields.description: JSON: the fields to put on the record the completion produces, for anything the task already knows and the worker should not have to retype — the laboratory a water sample goes to, the unit an inspection is of. Merged under whatever the completion itself supplies.
fields.label: Creates Record Data

fields.description: JSON: what this job consumes, as [{"item_code": "SPRAY-01", "qty": 5, "uom": "Litre", "warehouse": "Chemical Shed - OML"}]. v0.69.0. FOR A SPRAY THIS IS THE TANK MIX, stated when the task is raised because that is what the applicator is being sent to put on the block; for everything else it is whatever the completion says was used. Completing the task issues each line out of stock — one Material Issue per line, tagged back to this task — and a spray's REI and PHI windows are computed from the items in it. An issue that fails does NOT fail the completion: the work is the compliance record and the shed count is not.
fields.label: Materials Used

fields.description: JSON: what the completion's drawdown actually did — the Stock Entries written, and a warning for every line that could not be issued. Written by complete_farm_task and read by nobody else; it is here so the answer to 'did the chemical come off the count, and if not why not' lives on the task rather than only in the response somebody's phone got.
fields.label: Stock Drawdown

fields.description: When the spray this task IS actually finished. The anchor both intervals below are measured from — not the task's creation, not the sweep's clock. Written by the completion.
fields.label: Spray Completed At

fields.description: The restricted-entry interval's expiry, to the hour. Nobody enters this block without PPE until it passes (EPA WPS 40 CFR 170.407). Computed at completion from the LONGEST rei_hours in the tank — a mix is under the strictest product in it — and it is what the rei_active_block_entry rule reads. Empty means nothing sprayed here restricted entry.
fields.label: REI Expires At

fields.description: Which product in the tank set the REI above, so nobody has to reopen five labels to find out what they are waiting on.
fields.label: REI Source Item

fields.description: The first date this block may be harvested (FIFRA label pre-harvest interval; FDA tolerances 40 CFR 180). Computed at completion from the LONGEST phi_days in the tank, for the same reason the REI is. It is what the phi_harvest_window rule reads. Empty means nothing sprayed here restricted harvest.
fields.label: PHI Clears On

fields.description: Which product in the tank set the PHI above.
fields.label: PHI Source Item

fields.description: What the worker needs to know before they get there: where the key is, which breaker, who to ask. This is the field that decides whether a task is doable by somebody who was not in the room when it was written. A `Text` and not a `Small Text` since v0.79.0 — a foreman's account of a job runs longer than a line, and a field that runs out of room teaches people to write in note form. For an account written AFTER the fact, and for anything spoken rather than typed, see the `task_notes` table: this field is the brief, that one is the record.
fields.label: Instructions
Hierarchy and Links
fields.description: How this task relates to other tasks. A multi-day investigation is a parent with sub-tasks under it; two people who independently raised the same job are two tasks somebody links or merges.

The record this task is a step of. A DYNAMIC LINK and not a Link to Farm Task, because the thing with steps under it is as often an Accident Report as another task — an investigation's steps are 'interview the witness', 'photograph the scene', 'write the root cause', and the investigation is not a Farm Task. The same pair Farm Task already uses for location_doctype/location, for the same reason. A PARENT DOES NOT CLOSE WHILE A CHILD IS LIVE, which is what makes multi-day work stay open across shifts instead of being ticked off on the first evening.
fields.label: Parent Task

fields.description: Where the work went when this task was merged away. Set only on a task in the Merged state, and it is what makes that state readable rather than a dead end: somebody opening a duplicate six weeks later is told which record carries the evidence.
fields.label: Merged Into

fields.description: Other tasks this one is related to, duplicated by, or blocked by. WRITTEN ON BOTH SIDES — see Farm Task Link — so the relationship is visible from whichever record somebody opens.
fields.label: Linked Tasks
Narrative
fields.description: The account of what was done and why, appended over time. Multiple people may contribute over multiple days; entries are never edited, because a contemporaneous record that gets rewritten is not one.

Narrative entries, each with its author, its timestamp, and whether it was typed or spoken. A voice note transcribed on the handset lands here with `source_type = audio_transcription` and the recording attached, so the written record and the audio it came from stay together.
fields.label: Narrative Notes

fields.description: Which register the parent is in — 'Farm Task' for a step of a bigger job, 'Accident Report' for a step of an investigation.
fields.label: Parent DocType

name: Farm Task
